findings.quote: To simplify $\sqrt{n}$, look for the largest of these that divides $n$.
findings.problem: The shortcut fails when the largest perfect-square factor is above 100 or not in the list, and it gives no step to repeat. For sqrt(288) the largest listed divisor is 36, giving 6 sqrt(8) instead of 12 sqrt(2); for sqrt(432) it gives 6 sqrt(12) instead of 12 sqrt(3); for sqrt(242) no listed square divides, so the student may stop at sqrt(242) instead of 11 sqrt(2). On a multiple-choice item the student will not find the simplest form among the choices. The shortcut needs its limit (check the result again for a square factor, or allow squares above 100).
findings.source: content-checklist.md L27; writer-rules.md 'Rules added after round 1' rule 4 (word every shortcut with its limit); verified by arithmetic

findings.quote: Get one radical alone on one side.
findings.problem: The radical-equation procedure squares once and stops, and no example has two radicals. In an equation such as sqrt(3m+4) - sqrt(m+2) = 2, one squaring leaves a radical, and the procedure never says to isolate the remaining radical and raise to the power again. Solving radical equations is now in the lesson's goal (summary and brief item 'Finite radical equations and extraneous-root checking', curriculum class), and equations with two radicals are a standard application of that skill in the Grade 9 radical-equations competency.
findings.source: Brief thin item (acet-L069, ustet-L085, official curriculum); DepEd K to 12 Mathematics Curriculum Guide, Grade 9 Quarter 2, solving equations involving radical expressions; Grade 9 Week 8 activity sheet citing Workbook: Mathematics for Grade 9 pp. 108-111 (weak evidence, used only as corroboration)

findings.quote: Move everything to one side and factor.
findings.problem: Examples #9 and #11 depend on expanding a squared binomial, (x-2)^2 = x^2-4x+4, and on solving a quadratic by factoring and the zero-product property. The lesson neither teaches these nor names the prerequisite lessons that do (the algebra lessons on polynomials, for special products, and on quadratic equations). The lesson guide allows reuse only from an identified prerequisite, so the method used in the worked solutions has no traceable teaching.
findings.source: content-checklist.md L25; lesson-style-guide.md Teaching completeness (reuse rule); reader-rules.md 'Added after the Sol audit' (list every formula an example uses)
